newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-off $1 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-off $1 - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices early Tuesday were seen steady-$1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by continued light packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to plants could range from $57.50 to $58.50 per cwt.
Illinois top prices at plants could range from $56.00 to $57.00 while Indiana/Ohio tops at the plant could range from $56.00 to $57.00, sources in those areas said.
Weak packer demand was attributed to tightening operating margins as pork prices kept deteriorating in recent days, sources said.

Midday carlot pork traded slowly, with declines posted in pork bellies, trimmings and heavier-weight hams, according to USDA. There were 22.0 fabricated loads of fresh pork cuts and 8.0 loads of trimmings reported sold, USDA said.
Declines also were tied to larger-than-expected interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog marketings on Friday, which offset potential support from light movement expected Monday, market sources said.
Friday's marketings totaled 112,000 head, compared with that day's estimate of 105,000, USDA said. Monday's estimate was 105,000 head.
